'''Will Dockery Carpenter''' (July 13, 1930 – August 15, 2023) was an American scientist and philanthropist, who after earning a Ph.D. in plant physiology at [[Purdue University]] in 1958, began a 34-year professional career at [[Monsanto Company]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=69372539&privcapId=7756202&previousCapId=25240322&previousTitle=CUMBERLAND+PHARMACEUTICALS.|title=Will D. Carpenter: Executive Profile & Biography - Bloomberg|website=www.bloomberg.com}}</ref> during which time he headed the teams that tested and brought to market [[Lasso]] and [[Glyphosate|Roundup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.msstate.edu/newsroom/article/2015/09/msu-grad-student-now-intersection-industry-research/|title=MSU grad student now at intersection of industry, research|first=ITS Web Development|last=Team|date=3 September 2015|publisher=}}</ref> Because of his extensive knowledge and his notable participation in the Chemical Manufacturer's Association,<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fKddO3g6ZF8C&q=bob+mikulak%2Fwill+d+carpenter&pg=PA180|title=Biological Warfare: Modern Offense and Defense|last=Zilinskas|first=Raymond A.|date=2000|publisher=Lynne Rienner Publishers|isbn=9781555877613|location=|pages=180–83|language=en}}</ref> Carpenter became deeply involved in the efforts to obtain a worldwide chemical weapons treaty from 1978 through 2003. He was the primary representative for the American Chemical Manufacturers Association during those successful negotiations that led to the signing and ratification of the [[Chemical Weapons Convention]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.questia.com/newspaper/1P2-32977300/ex-executive-at-monsanto-backs-treaty-curbing-chemical|title="Ex-Executive at Monsanto Backs Treaty Curbing Chemical Weapons Crucial to Planet, He Warns" by Marianna Riley Of the Post-Dispatch - St Louis Post-Dispatch (MO), December 18, 1995|access-date=October 26, 2017|archive-date=March 24, 2018|via=[[Questia]]|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180324041154/https://www.questia.com/newspaper/1P2-32977300/ex-executive-at-monsanto-backs-treaty-curbing-chemical|work=St Louis Post-Dispatch|date=December 18, 1995|location=MO|url-status=dead}}</ref> testifying numerous times before Congress and working with chemical companies worldwide to help bring them on board with the terms of the treaty.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ebooksread.com/authors-eng/united-states-congress-senate-committee-on-fore/chemical-weapons-convention-treaty-doc-103-21--hearings-before-the-committee-tin/page-13-chemical-weapons-convention-treaty-doc-103-21--hearings-before-the-committee-tin.shtml |title=Data |website=ebooksread.com}}</ref>
Out of that convention, the [[Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons]] was formed, an organization that won the [[2013 Nobel Peace Prize]].  After the formation of the [[OPCW]], Carpenter was named as the U.S. representative to the Scientific Advisory Board.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://govinfo.library.unt.edu/ota/Ota_1/DATA/1993/9346.PDF |title= Data|website=govinfo.library.unt.edu}}</ref> He was awarded The AAAS Hilliard Roderick Prize for Excellence in Science, Arms Control, and International Security.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aaas.org/page/aaas-hilliard-roderick-prize |title= Prize listing |website=.aaas.org}}</ref> in 1992 for his participation on the [[Chemical Weapons Convention]]. Carpenter died at his home in [[Chesterfield, Missouri]] on August 15, 2023, at the age of 93.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Will Dockery Carpenter |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/stltoday/name/will-carpenter-obituary?id=52720419 |website=Legacy |access-date=31 December 2023}}</ref>
